MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 12, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on October 12, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 7, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs (arrived at 5:45 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:30 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  October 12, 2021
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Family Assistance Ministry 34th Annual Hunger Walk

  Mayor Kelley presented a certificate of commendation to CEO of Family Assistance
  Ministry Elizabeth Andrade.

P2. 2021 Disability Awareness Month Commendations by the Mission Viejo Diversity +
  Inclusion Task Force and City

  Mayor Kelley presented commendations to Director of Mount of Olives Adult Day Care
  Center Gaye Satterfield, and Ray Bueche of Esperanza High School.

P3. Proclaim the Month of October as "Breast Cancer Awareness Month" and Paint the
  Town Pink

  Mayor Kelley presented a proclamation to Executive Director of the Los Angeles Susan G.
  Komen Foundation Mark Pilon.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jerry Bryant, M.V.: Voiced concerns over the state mandates on affordable housing and the increase
in the City’s population and the amount of traffic this will cause. Encouraged the City Council to
fight the State.

Greg Nelson, M.V.: Asked when the Oso Creek Golf Course and Open Space Plan comes before
the City Council, that the reference to the Natatorium and the YMCA be removed since it is far out
of the realm of reality. Suggested that the City Council hold a town hall meeting regarding the plan
to clear the misconceptions that are floating around the community.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Cited the Brown Act and questioned the City Attorney on his interruption of
Martha Uriate’s public comments at a previous council meeting. Asked the Council what the plans
are if the YMCA does run out of space and outlined his opinions on the matter.

Cindy Ruhl, M.V.: Spoke out against the prospect of an apartment complex on the corner of
Marguerite and La Paz.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that at the last meeting the Mayor was unprofessional in allowing the
City Attorney to attack her with claims that she was misrepresenting and taking things out of
context. She voiced that executive staff was a disgrace and outlined examples from the last meeting.

City Manager Dennis Wilberg stated that the YMCA issue was covered extensively at the last
meeting and is viewable on the City Website. He reiterated there is no intention of tearing down
the YMCA. The situation is that the YMCA has expressed over the last couple of years that they
would like to expand their footprint in the City of Mission Viejo. City Manager Wilberg expressed
with regards to Mr. Gilbert and Ms. Schlicht, that he was pointing out that Mr. Gilbert did in fact
oppose the YMCA agreement which is stated in the Minutes. In regards to Ms. Schlicht, he noted
at the last meeting that she eliminated the key piece in the report which said everything related to

City Council Minutes  2  October 12, 2021
 the YMCA were simply ideas not proposals. Lastly, he said that the plan will be presented to the
City Council at the November 9 meeting.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister clarified that there is an application by Value
Rock regarding Garden Plaza. She stated that it is an incomplete application and it is her
understanding that it is being revised. Stressed that any discussion at this point is premature given
that the plans will change. Once the plans are complete it will be subject to design and review
committee, Planning and Transportation Commission, and City Council with Public Hearings. She
stated that there are private property rights, and the applicant doe have the right to submit an
application and a right to a fair hearing and due process. Lastly, she stated that this will most likely
be another two to three months before it is presented to the Planning Commission.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 28, 2021, as
  presented or as amended.

2.  Check Register Dated September 17, 2021 in the Amount of $362,017.77

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 24, 2021 in the Amount of $1,062,386.87

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2021

  Received and filed.

5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2021

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  October 12, 2021
 6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2021

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Via Escolar Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 22252)

  (1) Approved Construction Contract Change Order 1 with All American Asphalt, Inc. in the
  amount of $35,593.80 for additional work; (2) certified the completion of and accepted the
  improvements for the subject project; (3) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of
  Completion; (4) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County
  of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days,
  respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with the City; and (5) authorized the release of the final retention
  35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

9.  Updates to Wall of Recognition Policy

  Approved the Community Services Commission's recommended changes to the Wall of
  Recognition policy.

10. Road Closure Request from Trabuco Hills High School Instrumental Music Booster
  Club

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Trabuco Hills High School Instrumental
  Music Booster Club authorizing the closure of Mustang Run between Los Alisos Boulevard
  and Aguilar on Saturday, November 13, 2021.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARING

11. General Plan Amendment GPA2021-35 / Development Code Amendment DCA2021-19
  / Zone Change ZC2021-25 - City-initiated petitions, collectively referred to as the
  Proposed Amendments, related to the City’s state mandated Housing Element update to
  address the state’s 6th housing cycle covering the 2021-2029 Planning Period: (1)
  GPA2021-35 is proposed to amend the City’s General Plan Land Use Element and Land
  Use Policy Map to accommodate residential development as it pertains to 11 sites
  identified in the City’s draft General Plan Housing Element update, and to
  comprehensively update the Housing Element; (2) DCA2021-19 is proposed to amend
  the City’s Development Code to establish and define new high density zoning districts
  RPD_50 and RPD_80 (Residential Planned Development) including related land uses

City Council Minutes  4  October 12, 2021
   and development standards, and to address new state legislation related to accessory
  dwelling units, density bonus provisions, agricultural employee housing, low-barrier
  navigation centers, and transitional and supportive housing; and (3) ZC2021-25 is
  proposed to modify the City’s Zoning Map as it pertains to the 11 sites

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister, Planning Manager Larry Longenecker,
  and Consultant John Douglas gave the report.

  Mayor Kelley opened thy Public Hearing at 7:19 p.m.

  The following spoke:

  James Pugh, Newport Beach: Voiced that he is in favor of the Macy sight and the adoption
  of the Housing Element Update.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Outlined his concerns and opinion on the Housing Element.

  Ann Owens, Lake Forest.: Outlined her concerns and opinion on the Housing Element.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Outlined her concerns and opinion on the Housing Element.

  Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Outlined his concerns opinion on the Housing Element.

  Linda Tang, M.V.: Outlined her concerns and opinion on the Housing Element.

  The following provided written comments outlining their concerns and opinions of the
  Housing Element: Ramesh Joshi, Laguna Woods; Esther Brooks, M.V.; Tommie Kozlov,
  M.V.; Erin Schwarz, Foothill Ranch; Jon Achee, M.V.; Ilene Geiger, M.V.; Marilyn
  Schroeder, M.V.; Rona Henry; and Lyn Hayes, M.V.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 7:36 p.m.

  Motion by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Kelley to adopt Resolution 21-34
  Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2021-35 and Adopting the CEQA Addendum
  Document Prepared for the Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to adopt
  Urgency Ordinance 21-341 Pursuant to Government Code Section 36937(b) and Including
  the Facts Supporting the Urgency Declaration, Approving Development Code Amendment
  DCA2021-19, (i) Amending Title 9 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code to Establish and
  Define New High-Density Zoning Districts RPD-50 and RPD-80 (Residential Planned
  Development) Including Related Land Uses and Development Standards, and (ii) Addressing
  State Regulations Related to Accessory Dwelling Units, Density Bonus Provisions,
City Council Minutes  5  October 12, 2021
   Agriculture Employee Housing, Low-Barrier Navigation Centers, and Transitional and
  Supportive Housing, All Pursuant to the Requirements of the State Department of Housing
  and Community Development's Interpretation of State Law"; and adopt Urgency Ordinance
  21-342 Pursuant to Government Code Section 36937(b) and Including the Facts Supporting
  the Urgency Declaration, Approving Zone Change ZC2021-25, to Modify the City's Zoning
  Map as it Pertains to 11 Sites for Residential Development in Connection with the Amendment
  of the City's General Plan Housing Element, All Pursuant to the Requirements of the State
  Department of Housing and Community Development's Interpretation of State Law".
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Investment Advisory Commission Vacancy

  By Consensus the City Council continued this matter.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record..

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell outlined the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) and
Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) Board Meetings he has attending this past
week. Stated that there is a lot going on with the improvements on the freeway onramps and the
express way going up the 405 freeway to the County border.

Council Member Raths

No comments.

Council Member Sachs

No comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum shared that she attended the Armed Forces Football game at Mission
Viejo High School and Saddleback College Football game at their new stadium and she encouraged
residents to attend one of the football games to experience the new stadium. She attended and
participated in the Tee It Off for Marines Golf Tournament and had a wonderful time. Mayor Pro
Tem Bucknum stated she also attended the Bathgate Elementary School “Walk to School Day”.
City Council Minutes  6  October 12, 2021
 Finally, she attended the Orange County Tax Payers Association Roses and Radishes Annual Event
and explained that a rose is a good thing, and a radish is bad. Lastly, as a representative of the
Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) she accepted a radish which was due to
SCAG’s green print policy that is actually going to be bad for housing. Thanked staff for the Breast
Cancer Awareness Paint the Town Pink. Gave a shout out to the Rotary Club, The Kiwanis, and
The Elks Club for their participation in the Walk Against Drugs. Lastly, she spoke out about the
Aegean Heights neighborhood involving a party at an Airbnb that got out of control and asked if
staff could look into this.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum for attending the Saddleback College Stadium
Grand Opening as she attended an Eagle Court of Honor for Lauren Kiani and Isabelle Change
along with Council Member Raths. She mentioned that the discussion on park shade structures will
be discussed at the next meeting with the update of the budget. Mayor Kelley thanked Mission
Viejo High School for recognizing our veterans. She also attended the Tee It Up Golf Tournament
and had a wonderful time and commended the Marine Adoption Committee for raising over
$20,000 which will benefit our marines and sailors in Headquarters Battalion First Marin Division
at Camp Pendleton that the City adopted in 2006. Encouraged families to come out to the 2021
Walk Against Drugs this Saturday October 16.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:01 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in Memory of Caesar Michael del Prato to Tuesday, October
26, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

Approved at the meeting of October 26, 2021
